title: A call of an unexported helper with one argument more than its parameters is not a tail call
summary: `call step (n - 1) acc`, where `call f x = f x` is not exported by its unit, is not a tail call in native code: the type checker infers that the result of `call` may be local, and closure conversion puts a region around the over-application. A loop written so ends with `Stack_overflow`; bytecode and OCaml 5.4.0 run it in constant stack.
cause: `wrap_over_application` in `middle_end/flambda2/from_lambda/closure_conversion.ml` begins a region for an over-application when the result of the first application may be local and the result of the whole is not; the helper that is not exported is typed with a result that may be local.
